stories.title: Andhra pegs Cyclone Arnab damage at Rs 4,600 crore, seeks Centre aid for relief work

article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh has submitted a preliminary Cyclone Arnab damage report to the Centre.
The Rs 4,600 crore estimate underscores extensive infrastructure and agricultural losses.

Andhra Pradesh has submitted a preliminary report to the Centre estimating that very severe cyclonic storm Arnab caused damage worth Rs 4,600 crore in the state, Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu said on Friday, according to news agency Press Trust of India.
Naidu assured compensation and relief for affected families, farmers and fishermen.
He said seven people were killed in the cyclone despite precautionary measures and announced compensation of Rs 5 lakh for each bereaved family.

Speaking to reporters after visiting a cyclone shelter at Matrevu in West Godavari district, Naidu said the government was working to restore essential services and assist people who had suffered losses.
"The preliminary assessment puts the damage caused by very severe cyclonic storm Arnab at Rs 4,600 crore.
We have submitted the report to the Centre and will ensure compensation and relief reach all affected families, farmers and fishermen," Naidu said, according to PTI.
He said the government had coordinated preparations across departments before the cyclone.
Officials were kept on alert through repeated teleconferences and overnight reviews.
The administration also monitored the possibility of heavy inflows into reservoirs and tanks to prepare for potential flooding.
Power infrastructure suffered extensive damage, with more than 15,000 electricity poles uprooted across the affected areas.

stories.headline: Israel election: Netanyahu falls short of majority; what happens next?
stories.title: Israel election: Netanyahu falls short of majority; what happens next?
stories.summary: Israel’s election has produced a political deadlock. With all votes counted by October 30, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc has 53 seats in the 120-member Knesset, while the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot has 48. Arab-led parties have secured 19 seats, their strongest showing in an Israeli election.Neither of the two main blocs has the 61 seats required for a parliamentary majority. The result leaves the Arab parties with a potentially decisive role in determining who forms the next government, although the opposition has so far been reluctant to work with them.Why this Israeli election mattersThis is Israel’s first parliamentary election since the Hamas-led attacks of October 7, 2023, and the wars that followed in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran. Netanyahu has remained at the centre of international attention since the attacks. His government’s military campaign in Gaza has drawn widespread international criticism, and the International Criminal Court issued an arrest warrant for him in November 2024 over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity.The election is widely being seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s leadership, his government’s handling of the October 7 security failures, and the direction of the country’s wars. His Likud party emerged as the largest in parliament with 27 seats, but his wider bloc fell from 68 seats in the outgoing Knesset to 53.Also Read: Against the tide: Lula’s electoral turnaround shows the left can still prevailWho is Gadi Eisenkot and what does he want?Eisenkot, 66, is a former chief of staff of the Israel Defence Forces and leads the Yashar party. He campaigned on security, political reform, and ending Netanyahu’s tenure. His bloc includes Naftali Bennett’s B’Yachad, Yair Golan’s Democrats and Avigdor Lieberman’s Yisrael Beytenu.Security is central to Eisenkot’s platform. He has called for a new national security strategy and the dismantling of Hamas’s military capabilities. He has also pledged an independent investigation into the October 7 attacks and the decisions that preceded them. Domestically, he has backed wider military or national service, including for ultra-Orthodox Jewish men, and reforms to strengthen public institutions.But a change of prime minister would not necessarily mean a major change in Israel’s position on Palestinians. Eisenkot has opposed the establishment of a Palestinian state and has argued for continued Israeli security control in Gaza. His approach differs from Netanyahu’s in its emphasis on a new security strategy and political accountability, but both leaders have taken hard positions on Hamas.Also Read: flydubai cockpit attack: Modi, Netanyahu call Indian pilot Smit Machchhar ‘hero’Why are Arab parties important?The Joint List and Ra’am won a combined 19 seats, their strongest showing in an Israeli election. Arab citizens make up about a fifth of Israel’s population, and the turnout gave the parties significant parliamentary weight.Their seats could help Eisenkot reach a majority. His 48-seat bloc, together with the 19 Arab-party seats, would have 67. But several parties in his alliance have ruled out relying on Arab parties to form a government. Eisenkot himself campaigned against including them in a coalition.Netanyahu has also sought to make such cooperation politically difficult. He has previously alleged that Arab parties had stolen votes, without presenting evidence. Israel’s election authorities rejected claims of systematic electoral violations, while the Shin Bet said its investigation was not intended to cast suspicion on Arab voters as a group.Ra’am joined Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid’s governing coalition in 2021, the first time an independent Arab party became part of an Israeli government. However, that coalition lasted 18 months.Trump, Gaza, and IranIsrael is a key US ally at a time when the region remains unsettled by the wars in Gaza and Iran. US President Donald Trump endorsed Netanyahu ahead of the election. After the vote, Trump told Axios that Netanyahu was in “pretty good shape” and said he believed his endorsement had made a difference.Asked whether he would get involved in efforts to form a unity government led by Netanyahu, Trump said: “I will take a look.”For Gaza, however, the elections are unlikely to produce any immediate change. Reuters quoted Jonathan Panikoff, a former US deputy national intelligence officer for West Asia, as saying it was “hard to imagine any real daylight” between a future Israeli leadership and Trump if the US president decided to escalate the confrontation with Iran. Reuters also reported that analysts saw little reason to expect a sweeping change in Israeli policy towards the Palestinians, regardless of how the next government is formed.What happens next?The new Knesset is scheduled to be sworn in on November 10, but the formation of a government could take several more weeks. After the final results are formally submitted on November 4, President Isaac Herzog will consult party leaders and nominate a lawmaker to try to form a coalition. The candidate will have 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, to secure the support of at least 61 lawmakers. Netanyahu will remain caretaker prime minister until a new government is approved by parliament.Washington-based think tank The Atlantic Council’s experts in their analysis have described the election as having “solved very little”. Former US ambassador to Israel Daniel Shapiro said a “clear majority of Israelis registered their desire for a different government”. But fellow Atlantic Council expert Gina Abercrombie-Winstanley offered a more cautious reading: Netanyahu “has not been thoroughly repudiated”, as Likud continues to be the largest party.Netanyahu could try to bring members of the opposition into a unity government, while Eisenkot could seek support from Arab parties outside a formal coalition. Both options would require leaders to reconsider campaign commitments.

stories.title: Andhra State Election Commission agrees to publish candidate affidavits online following PIL

article_sentences: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links.

The Andhra Pradesh High Court on Friday, October 30, disposed of a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) after the State Election Commission (APSEC) confirmed it has issued orders to publish contesting candidates' nomination papers and affidavits online for upcoming local body elections.
With the state set to vote on Sunday, November 1, the portal had not published affidavit details at the time of disposal of the PIL.
The PIL in question was filed amid the ongoing violence in Andhra’s urban local body polls.
The case was heard by a division bench comprising Chief Justice Lisa Gill and Justice Challa Gunaranjan.

The government pleader representing APSEC informed Chief Justice Lisa Gill that the commission issued an official order the previous day directing that candidate affidavits and nomination details be uploaded and displayed on the APSEC portal.
The petition was filed earlier in the week by Siva Karthik Valaparla, a resident of Nuzvid, Krishna district.
The petitioner had approached the court seeking directions to compel the state election body to establish an online candidate disclosure system.
On October 17, Siva Karthik submitted a formal representation via email and post to the State Election Commissioner.

Drawing a parallel to the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) candidate affidavit portal, he had requested APSEC to create a dedicated web portal to publish nomination papers and affidavits organised by district, local body, ward, and candidate name to foster transparency and informed voting in local body polls.
In its written response dated October 23, the APSEC initially rejected the request.

The commission cited Section 36 of the Andhra Pradesh Municipal Corporations Act and the AP Municipalities (Conduct of Election of Members) Rules, stating that governing election laws only mandated physical submission of nomination papers directly to Returning.

stories.headline: PM Modi lays foundation stone, inaugurates and dedicates to nation projects worth over Rs 14,000 crore in Banaskantha, Gujarat
stories.title: PM Modi lays foundation stone, inaugurates and dedicates to nation projects worth over Rs 14,000 crore in Banaskantha, Gujarat
stories.summary: Gujarat, Oct 30: Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone, inaugurated, and dedicated to the nation development projects worth over ₹14,000 crore today in Banaskantha, Gujarat. Speaking on the sacred soil of Mother Amba shortly after Navratri, he unveiled multiple initiatives for women, children, farmers, and cattle rearers, while also disbursing a fresh installment of the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi to tens of millions of small farmers nationwide. Describing farmers and annadatas as among the strongest pillars of a Viksit Bharat, the Prime Minister stated that the government has consistently prioritized their welfare and empowerment, increasing the national agricultural budget more than fivefold compared to 2013-14. Noting that the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi has become an integral part of small farmers' lives, he highlighted that over 1,000 crore rupees have been deposited into the accounts of more than 50 lakh farmers in Gujarat, including nearly 50 crore rupees for lakhs of farming families in Banaskantha. “Today, an amount of more than 18 thousand crore rupees has been sent into the accounts of about 10 crore farmers,” noted PM Modi. Highlighting that government policies over recent years have delivered or saved more than 50 lakh crore rupees for farmers, the Prime Minister cited the first of five key examples by pointing out that nearly 4.5 lakh crore rupees have been transferred directly into the bank accounts of small farmers under the PM Kisan Samman Nidhi. He observed that small farmers constitute over 85 percent of the farming community and our government cared for such small farmers and provided them help through PM Kisan Samman Nidhi,” asserted PM Modi. Pointing to the sharp surge in global fertilizer prices amid international uncertainty over the past few years, the Prime Minister emphasized that his farmer-centric government shielded cultivators from the price hike. “The government spent about 16 lakh crore rupees on this,” noted PM Modi. The Prime Minister underscored that the government fulfilled its MSP commitment. “In the past 12 years, wheat and paddy farmers have received more than 24 lakh crore rupees as MSP,” observed PM Modi. Spotlighting the strong security shield provided to cultivators through the PM Fasal Bima Yojana, the Prime Minister stated that farmers have received over 2 lakh crore rupees in crop insurance compensation over the last 10 to 12 years, alongside continuous efforts to reduce irrigation costs through the expanding role of the PM-KUSUM scheme. He explained that the distribution of nearly 12 lakh solar pumps under the scheme has generated additional electricity and saved lakhs of farmers the expense of purchasing over 80 crore liters of diesel, bringing the total financial benefit or savings from just these five major schemes and decisions to 50 lakh crore rupees. “These 50 lakh crore rupees have increased the income of the country's farmers and enhanced the capability of agriculture in India,” asserted PM Modi. Emphasizing that agriculture is both a tradition and a vital part of Indian culture, the Prime Minister stated that the government has extensively integrated science and technology into farming and animal husbandry over the past 12 years. He cited the Soil Health Card as a prime example that resolved farmers' earlier difficulties in determining the exact type and quantity of fertilizer required for their fields, modernizing agricultural practices across the country. “Today more than 26 crore Soil Health Cards are with the country's farmers,” noted PM Modi. Acknowledging that changing weather patterns pose a major challenge to cultivators, the Prime Minister stated that the government is continuously striving to provide farmers with new climate-resilient seed varieties. “In recent years, about three thousand new varieties of seeds have been made available to farmers,” observed PM Modi. Highlighting animal husbandry as a vital component of the rural economy with massive participation from rural women, the Prime Minister emphasized the integration of science and technology into the dairy and livestock sector over the past decade. He explained that superior animal breeds boost milk yields while timely vaccination and medical treatment curb losses from disease. “Meaning, if the animal is healthy, the earnings of my livestock-rearing brothers and sisters will also increase,” affirmed PM Modi. Spotlighting the Rashtriya Gokul Mission's role in promoting the conservation and scientific breeding of indigenous livestock, the Prime Minister noted that the newly built research center in Banaskantha will strengthen this mission by conserving and improving the quality of indigenous cow breeds like Gir, Sahiwal, and Kankrej, as well as buffalo breeds like Mehsana, Murrah, and Jaffarabadi, serving as the country's first such facility for the Kankrej breed. He explained that when a farmer wishes to pass down the traits of a high-yielding, low-maintenance, healthy cow to future generations, modern technologies like IVF increase the probability of transferring those superior qualities. “The livestock farmer will get its direct benefit,” noted PM Modi. Stating that protecting livestock from ailments like foot-and-mouth disease is a key priority because such illnesses impact both animal health and milk yields, the Prime Minister highlighted the launch of a nationwide free vaccination drive. He pointed out that about 150 crore vaccine doses have been administered so far, providing free vaccination to the livestock of over 8 crore farmers. “This has also reduced the financial burden on livestock farmers,” observed PM Modi. Pointing to the visible impact of these interventions on dairy output, the Prime Minister noted that average daily milk yield per cow or buffalo has risen from under 5 liters in 2013-14 to nearly 8 liters today, giving India the fastest milk productivity growth rate in the world and benefiting rural farming families. “India is number one in the world in milk production,” remarked PM Modi. Expressing the government's resolve to help livestock rearers earn from cow dung as well as milk, the Prime Minister stated that infrastructure is being built with the vital support of institutions like Banas Dairy to produce biogas, bio-CNG, and organic fertilizer from dung and farm residue, marked by the foundation stone laying of two bio-CNG plants today. He underscored the clear objective of keeping livestock healthy, increasing milk yields, and ensuring the complete utilization of dung. “We are making animal husbandry not just a tradition, but a powerful instrument for increasing farmers' income and enriching villages,” asserted PM Modi. Explaining that the government has worked with a holistic approach over recent years to ensure rural prosperity, the Prime Minister pointed to the vast expansion of the fisheries sector and the promotion of cooperatives within it. “You will be glad to hear that India's seafood exports have more than doubled,” noted PM Modi. Highlighting beekeeping as another major avenue of supplementary income for farmers, the Prime Minister noted that honey production has doubled over the past 12 years and lauded the growing contribution of women's Self-Help Groups in driving this Madhu Kranti. “You will be proud to know that our country has become the second-largest exporter of natural honey,” observed PM Modi. Recalling that on October 7 he completed 25 years of service as the head of a government after first taking oath on October 7, 2001, the Prime Minister reflected on the immense love and guidance he received from every Gujarati at a time when he knew nothing of government offices or official files. He expressed gratitude to the people for entrusting a person from a poor family, whose ancestors never even dreamed of becoming a village sarpanch, with the responsibility of serving first Gujarat and then the nation. “And even more than love, every single Gujarati has taught me and led me on the right path,” remarked PM Modi. Stating that he only knew the two guiding principles of serving the nation through public service and developing the country through Gujarat's development while learning everything else from the people, the Prime Minister credited citizens for whatever he has achieved for the nation. “For this, I will remain indebted to you for life, and until the last moment of life, I will remain engaged in your service,” affirmed PM Modi. Reminding older citizens of the acute water and electricity shortages that plagued the region 25 years ago, the Prime Minister recalled how the people heeded his appeal to conserve both resources and transformed their circumstances so thoroughly that those old hardships now remain only in memories. “I will say the same thing to you again today, that we have to save water, save electricity,” urged PM Modi. Highlighting how Narmada waters and modern technologies like drip irrigation have transformed Banaskantha and made its potatoes world-famous alongside Banas Dairy's expansion of the cooperative movement to Kashi and beyond, the Prime Minister pointed out that the capacity of the potato plant that makes French fries has also been increased to enable greater procurement of potatoes. “This is a very big facility for potato farmers,” noted PM Modi. Detailing the ongoing cluster development program for fruit and vegetable cultivators under which 12 clusters were approved today for tomato, potato, chili, grapes, banana, onion, orange, pomegranate, and cocoa, the Prime Minister stated that farmers are receiving subsidies to plant new orchards and rejuvenate old ones. “The two clusters received in North Gujarat will greatly benefit the potato farmers of Banaskantha and Sabarkantha,” observed PM Modi. Listing several major infrastructure projects inaugurated or initiated for Gujarat's development today, the Prime Minister highlighted the flagging off of two new rail services, the Ahmedabad-Varanasi Sabarmati Express and the Mehsana-Becharaji-Sabarmati MEMU train, alongside the expansion of the Ahmedabad Metro with foundation stones laid for metro projects connecting GIFT City and the airport. “The Ahmedabad-Mehsana highway is now going to become eight-lane from four-lane,” noted PM Modi. Spotlighting new social welfare infrastructure launched for the children of the state today, the Prime Minister noted that over 4,000 modern Anganwadis have been inaugurated across Gujarat. “This will benefit about 4 lakh children and pregnant mothers,” observed PM Modi. Stating that every such developmental effort is aimed at building a developed India as every farmer, youth, sister, and daughter marches forward with the resolve of a Viksit Bharat, the Prime Minister remarked that unfortunately some elements dislike this progress and wish to see the nation in difficulty. “When crises befall the country, they feel happy,” remarked PM Modi. Citing the ongoing war around Iran and the Gulf countries as a recent example where India stood united to face the situation while certain elements spread rumors to scare farmers about fertilizer shortages and women about gas supplies, the Prime Minister stated that their plan was to trigger chaos in the country to defame him. “When India was engaged in facing this unitedly, then these people kept spreading rumors,” remarked PM Modi. Reminding the farming community of his solemn assurance to stand firmly beside them, the Prime Minister pointed out that the government prevented any scarcity of agricultural inputs despite the ongoing conflict. Noting that the war caused global prices of fertilizers and raw chemicals to skyrocket, the Prime Minister highlighted that the government shielded Indian cultivators from the burden, providing a bag of urea that costs 3,000 rupees globally for under 300 rupees in India, and supplying a bag of DAP that exceeds 5,000 rupees internationally for just 1,350 rupees. “The country is providing this help so that our farmer is empowered, and the farmer's life becomes better,” affirmed PM Modi. article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently reserved judgment on the issue whether the period spent to acquire Ph.D. can be counted towards teaching experience for the appointment as Associate Professor as per the norms of the University Grants Commission.

A bench comprising Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Manmohan heard the petitions filed by the UGC as well as Professor Joseph Skaria challenging the Kerala High Court's 2023 judgment which upheld the appointment of Priya Varghese, wife of CPI(M) KK Ragesh who was the Private Secretary to the then Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, in the Kannur University.

The issue arose after Dr.Joseph Skariah, who was ranked after Varghese in the Rank List, had filed the writ petition challenging the inclusion of Varghese in the List, stating that she was not qualified for the post of Associate Professor as she did not have the prescribed 8 years of teaching experience.
A single judge of the Kerala High Court found that Varghese didn't have the requisite teaching experience and directed Kannur University to re-examine her credentials.
This was challenged by Varghese before the division bench, which held it in her favour.
Against this, the aggrieved candidate and the UGC appealed to the Supreme Court.
"The time taken by candidates to acquire M.Phil.
and/or Ph.D. Degree shall not be considered as teaching/research experience to be claimed for appointment to the teaching positions.

Further, the period of active service spent on pursuing a Research Degree simultaneously with teaching assignment without taking any kind of leave, shall be counted as teaching experience for the purpose of direct recruitment/promotion.

Regular faculty members up to twenty percent of the total faculty strength (excluding faculty on medical/maternity leave) shall be allowed by their respective institutions to take study leave for pursuing Ph.D. degree."
He submitted that Regulation 3.1.1 is divided into three parts; the first is a general provision applying to all "candidates".
Whereas the second part extends to those in active service, and the third part is merely a guideline for regular faculty.

stories.title: MCA clarifies role in NCLT appointments after Supreme Court flags interference
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 30: In the light of certain news reports concerning personnel matters relating to the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) made by the Supreme Court, the respective roles of the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) and the NCLT may be seen in the context of the distinct responsibilities assigned to them. In a statement issued, the Ministry of Corporate Affairs said the MCA only performs the administrative role in the conduct of the appointment process for the 63 Judicial and Technical Members of the NCLT. The NCLT independently undertakes the process for appointment and management of its officers and staff, including Deputy Registrars, Court Officers, Stenographers, Office Assistants and Multi-Tasking Staff. The Government delegated this responsibility to the NCLT vide notification dated 14 October 2019, with a view to ensuring its effective and independent functioning.

stories.headline: Why the IDBI Bank sale matters beyond Rs52,878 crore price tag
stories.title: Why the IDBI Bank sale matters beyond Rs52,878 crore price tag
stories.summary: As the long-delayed sale of IDBI Bank comes to a close, the significance of the ₹52,878 crore transaction extends far beyond the cheque that Fairfax is set to write. The deal marks the government’s most consequential strategic disinvestment since Air India in 2022. It also offers a rare example of a complex privatisation reaching fruition after years of regulatory, operational and investor-related hurdles.On October 14, the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs approved the sale of IDBI Bank to Canada-based Fairfax Financial Holding. According to the deal contour, Fairfax Financial Holdings will get 60.72 percent stake in IDBI Bank for ₹52,878 crore. Of the total sale, the government will sell 30.48 percent and retain 15 percent, while the Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) will sell 30.24 percent and keep 19 percent. The government’s share of the proceeds is expected to be about ₹26,000 crore.The IDBI deal with Fairfax delivers the government’s most significant strategic disinvestment since Air India and provides a much-needed boost to FY27 divestment receipts. More importantly, it signals that large-scale state-owned assets can still attract long-term capital, providing fresh momentum to India’s privatisation agenda at a time when the government’s disinvestment programme has struggled to meet its targets.Also Read: Markets fund 74% of Centre’s disinvestment; strategic sales under 10%However, the transaction also lays bare a persistent weakness in India’s privatisation plan. The government’s disinvestment programme remains heavily reliant on a handful of marquee transactions to meet ambitious asset-sale targets, raising questions about the depth and sustainability of the broader privatisation pipeline.“The IDBI sale shows India’s privatisation programme can deliver, but slowly, case by case, and with the state keeping a minority foothold rather than leaving outright. The IDBI stake sale can become a template where a foreign buyer can control an Indian bank. It also emboldens the government’s strategic sale privatisation programme, especially in public sector banks,” says Garima Kapoor, deputy head of research and economist-institutional equities, Elara Securities.For market observers, the IDBI Bank sale is significant not only because of its size but also because it offers a potential blueprint for future strategic sales. The structure balances private-sector control with continued government participation, a model that could make privatisation financially more palatable.According to Manish Aggarwal, partner and leader, financial services and infrastructure transactions, Deloitte India, it is one of the largest and most complex strategic disinvestments undertaken by the government. The IDBI Bank deal marks a significant milestone in India’s reform journey, advances the government’s disinvestment objectives and reinforces the country’s position as an attractive destination for long-term foreign investment, according to him.“The deal is structured very well… the foreign investor gets management control, brings in capital, expertise to grow the bank, and the government rides this upside through its residual stake. With global investors continuing to back India’s growth potential with the largest foreign direct investment in the sector despite an uncertain geopolitical environment is testimony to India’s political stability, continued focus on reforms and belief in the highest growth rates of our economy,” says Aggarwal. He adds the deal is also an important step in attracting long-term foreign capital into a sector that will play a critical role in supporting India’s next phase of growth.Analysts at Choice Institutional Equities agree: “Closing a sale that has dragged on for years is a genuine win.”However, it also exposes the privatisation programme’s continued dependence on infrequent, big-ticket strategic sales. The analysts explain that one transaction delivering roughly a third of the full-year target underscores how thin and lumpy the disinvestment pipeline remains. “Leaning on a single large ticket to rescue the FY27 number looks like a familiar pattern rather than a structural fix. The terms are also accommodating to the buyer, with a 15-year runway to pare the stake and two years to resolve the CSB Bank overlap. Execution risk now shifts to regulatory clearances and completion timing, and budget math that leans on one closing stays fragile,” they say. In 2018, Fairfax had acquired 51 percent in CSB Bank (earlier known as Catholic Syrian Bank). Currently, it holds 40 percent in CSB Bank.According to the terms of the deal, Fairfax must cut its holding to 26 percent over 15 years and exit or merge its 40 percent stake in CSB Bank within two years. The government plans to divest its remaining 15 percent stake in IDBI Bank through market sale, while LIC will manage its residual holding, paving the way for a gradual transition to private ownership.Also Read: Fairfax to buy 60.7% of IDBI Bank for Rs52,878 crore in biggest banking FDIRoad to privatisationThe IDBI stake sale is expected to fill up the government’s coffers and the divestment target for this fiscal is likely to be met for the first time in eight years. In the first five months (April-August) of FY27, the government had achieved nearly 70 percent of its annual divestment target, raising about ₹55,700 crore, before accounting for the IDBI Bank stake sale. The contrast with recent years is striking. Between FY20 and FY26, the government had hit, on average, just 33 percent of its budgeted disinvestment targets, reflecting persistent challenges in executing strategic sales and a reliance on stake dilutions and buybacks to bridge the gap.Kapoor says the share sale in IDBI Bank is expected to lift FY27 disinvestment proceeds to ₹82,301 crore, above the ₹80,000 crore target, offering critical buffer at a time when government finances are facing stress due to higher subsidies and excise duty cuts on petrol and diesel. In May, the government approved the strategic sale of Indian Medicines Pharmaceutical Corporation to Delhi-based pharma manufacturer Skymap Pharmaceuticals Private for ₹121.01 crore.Proceeds from the sale of 6.5 percent in LIC (₹31,500 crore) form a large chunk of the disinvestment in the current fiscal. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) had granted LIC a three-year extension in May 2024 to achieve the 10 percent free float target. By launching the offer-for-sale in August, the government met the mandated threshold nine months ahead of the deadline.India’s privatisation push gained momentum with the sale of Air India in 2022, and the government’s broader strategy of reducing its presence in non-strategic sectors. However, execution has lagged ambition. Several proposed strategic sales, including BPCL and Shipping Corporation of India, have faced delays because of regulatory, legal and market-related hurdles.As a result, the government has frequently fallen short of its divestment targets. It has relied more on minority stake sales and buybacks by public sector companies than outright privatisation. Against this backdrop, the IDBI Bank transaction stands out.Also Read: IDBI Bank divestment: Strong optics and no hidden surprises lure potential buyersWhat’s in it for Fairfax?For Fairfax, the ₹81-per-share offer provides a pathway to acquire a banking franchise at a valuation that meets the government’s sale criteria while securing management control of one of India’s larger lenders. “Since the winning best offer bid of ₹81 per share was above the benchmark price, as well as fair value estimates of both the independent valuation agencies, it was adjudged to be reasonable and approved,” says a government statement to the stock exchanges.However, the valuation could not win market investors’ confidence. The ₹81-per share was lower than the closing price of ₹90.16 on October 14 when the deal was announced. Since then, investors are dumping shares of IDBI Bank in the secondary markets. The stock is down 14 percent in less than 10 days, indicating investor concerns over the takeover valuations.For Fairfax, the acquisition is a long-term vision than just a strategic buy. “Fairfax’s objective in buying the 60.72 percent interest in IDBI Bank is to make it, over time, a leading global Indian bank headquartered in India,” according to a company statement.Fairfax’s bet extends beyond banking. It is still awaiting approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and needs to comply with prescribed regulatory conditions to complete the IDBI Bank deal. However, the Prem Watsa-led company has chalked out its long-term plan for the combined entity. It wants to create a platform to build a diversified financial services franchise spanning insurance, wealth management and investment banking, while capitalising on India’s long-term credit expansion and financialisation.Fairfax plans to combine all its stakes in Digit (Go Digit Life Insurance and Go Digit General Insurance) and IIFL Capital Services to IDBI Bank. Fairfax owns a 30.2 percent stake in IIFL Capital Services and 49 percent stake in Digit.“Combining IDBI Bank, Digit and IIFL Capital would create an entity that is well-positioned to participate in the continued growth and success of Indian markets, and we expect it to provide meaningful and significant benefits to Indian consumers and businesses, as well as to IDBI Bank, Digit, IIFL Capital and to Fairfax for many decades to come,” says Prem Watsa, chairman and CEO, Fairfax, in a statement.Watsa feels that a newly revitalised IDBI Bank that can also offer clients insurance products through Digit, and investment banking and wealth management services through IIFL Capital would be in a competitive position to take advantage of India’s growth.Following the IDBI transaction, Fairfax expects the operations of the combined company to be led by Rakesh Sharma, managing director and CEO of the bank. It also plans to include in the IDBI Bank’s leadership group CVR Rajendran, former CEO of CSB Bank, as well as NS Kannan, former MD and CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Company, and CFO of ICICI Bank, who will act as chairman. All this is subject to approval from the RBI, says a company statement.Fairfax does not expect any change in the governance, management or operating structure of either Digit or IIFL Capital due to the merged entity.Post the stake sale announcement, Crisil has placed its rating on the long-term debt instruments of IDBI Bank on ‘rating watch with positive implications’ and has reaffirmed its ‘Crisil A1+’ rating on the certificate of deposit programme. The ratings agency believes that IDBI Bank is likely to benefit from Fairfax’s majority ownership and strategic commitment.“Over the past few years, IDBI Bank has demonstrated a sustained improvement in its standalone credit profile, reflected in improved asset quality, healthy profitability and comfortable capitalisation profile. The proposed acquisition has the potential to further strengthen the bank’s business profile by providing access to Fairfax’s broader financial services ecosystem, including insurance and wealth management businesses,” Crisil says.

It also emboldens the government’s strategic sale privatisation programme, especially in public sector banks,” says Garima Kapoor, deputy head of research and economist-institutional equities, Elara Securities.
For market observers, the IDBI Bank sale is significant not only because of its size but also because it offers a potential blueprint for future strategic sales.
The structure balances private-sector control with continued government participation, a model that could make privatisation financially more palatable.

According to Manish Aggarwal, partner and leader, financial services and infrastructure transactions, Deloitte India, it is one of the largest and most complex strategic disinvestments undertaken by the government.

The IDBI Bank deal marks a significant milestone in India’s reform journey, advances the government’s disinvestment objectives and reinforces the country’s position as an attractive destination for long-term foreign investment, according to him.
“The deal is structured very well… the foreign investor gets management control, brings in capital, expertise to grow the bank, and the government rides this upside through its residual stake.

With global investors continuing to back India’s growth potential with the largest foreign direct investment in the sector despite an uncertain geopolitical environment is testimony to India’s political stability, continued focus on reforms and belief in the highest growth rates of our economy,” says Aggarwal.
He adds the deal is also an important step in attracting long-term foreign capital into a sector that will play a critical role in supporting India’s next phase of growth.

Analysts at Choice Institutional Equities agree: “Closing a sale that has dragged on for years is a genuine win.” However, it also exposes the privatisation programme’s continued dependence on infrequent, big-ticket strategic sales.
The analysts explain that one transaction delivering roughly a third of the full-year target underscores how thin and lumpy the disinvestment pipeline remains.
“Leaning on a single large ticket to rescue the FY27 number looks like a familiar pattern rather than a structural fix.
The terms are also accommodating to the buyer, with a 15-year runway to pare the stake and two years to resolve the CSB Bank overlap.
Execution risk now shifts to regulatory clearances and completion timing, and budget math that leans on one closing stays fragile,” they say.
The IDBI stake sale is expected to fill up the government’s coffers and the divestment target for this fiscal is likely to be met for the first time in eight years.
The contrast with recent years is striking.

Kapoor says the share sale in IDBI Bank is expected to lift FY27 disinvestment proceeds to ₹82,301 crore, above the ₹80,000 crore target, offering critical buffer at a time when government finances are facing stress due to higher subsidies and excise duty cuts on petrol and diesel.
In May, the government approved the strategic sale of Indian Medicines Pharmaceutical Corporation to Delhi-based pharma manufacturer Skymap Pharmaceuticals Private for ₹121.01 crore.
By launching the offer-for-sale in August, the government met the mandated threshold nine months ahead of the deadline.
India’s privatisation push gained momentum with the sale of Air India in 2022, and the government’s broader strategy of reducing its presence in non-strategic sectors.
However, execution has lagged ambition.
Several proposed strategic sales, including BPCL and Shipping Corporation of India, have faced delays because of regulatory, legal and market-related hurdles.
As a result, the government has frequently fallen short of its divestment targets.
It has relied more on minority stake sales and buybacks by public sector companies than outright privatisation.
Against this backdrop, the IDBI Bank transaction stands out.
What’s in it for Fairfax?

For Fairfax, the ₹81-per-share offer provides a pathway to acquire a banking franchise at a valuation that meets the government’s sale criteria while securing management control of one of India’s larger lenders.

“Since the winning best offer bid of ₹81 per share was above the benchmark price, as well as fair value estimates of both the independent valuation agencies, it was adjudged to be reasonable and approved,” says a government statement to the stock exchanges.
However, the valuation could not win market investors’ confidence.
The ₹81-per share was lower than the closing price of ₹90.16 on October 14 when the deal was announced.
Since then, investors are dumping shares of IDBI Bank in the secondary markets.
The stock is down 14 percent in less than 10 days, indicating investor concerns over the takeover valuations.
For Fairfax, the acquisition is a long-term vision than just a strategic buy.
Fairfax’s bet extends beyond banking.
It is still awaiting approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and needs to comply with prescribed regulatory conditions to complete the IDBI Bank deal.
However, the Prem Watsa-led company has chalked out its long-term plan for the combined entity.

It wants to create a platform to build a diversified financial services franchise spanning insurance, wealth management and investment banking, while capitalising on India’s long-term credit expansion and financialisation.
Fairfax plans to combine all its stakes in Digit (Go Digit Life Insurance and Go Digit General Insurance) and IIFL Capital Services to IDBI Bank.

“Combining IDBI Bank, Digit and IIFL Capital would create an entity that is well-positioned to participate in the continued growth and success of Indian markets, and we expect it to provide meaningful and significant benefits to Indian consumers and businesses, as well as to IDBI Bank, Digit, IIFL Capital and to Fairfax for many decades to come,” says Prem Watsa, chairman and CEO, Fairfax, in a statement.

Watsa feels that a newly revitalised IDBI Bank that can also offer clients insurance products through Digit, and investment banking and wealth management services through IIFL Capital would be in a competitive position to take advantage of India’s growth.
Following the IDBI transaction, Fairfax expects the operations of the combined company to be led by Rakesh Sharma, managing director and CEO of the bank.

It also plans to include in the IDBI Bank’s leadership group CVR Rajendran, former CEO of CSB Bank, as well as NS Kannan, former MD and CEO of ICICI Prudential Life Company, and CFO of ICICI Bank, who will act as chairman.
All this is subject to approval from the RBI, says a company statement.
Fairfax does not expect any change in the governance, management or operating structure of either Digit or IIFL Capital due to the merged entity.
Post the stake sale announcement, Crisil has placed its rating on the long-term debt instruments of IDBI Bank on ‘rating watch with positive implications’ and has reaffirmed its ‘Crisil.
A1+’ rating on the certificate of deposit programme.
The ratings agency believes that IDBI Bank is likely to benefit from Fairfax’s majority ownership and strategic commitment.

“Over the past few years, IDBI Bank has demonstrated a sustained improvement in its standalone credit profile, reflected in improved asset quality, healthy profitability and comfortable capitalisation profile.

The proposed acquisition has the potential to further strengthen the bank’s business profile by providing access to Fairfax’s broader financial services ecosystem, including insurance and wealth management businesses,” Crisil says.

stories.title: Supreme Court asks Centre to take measures against online misuse of court feeds
stories.summary: Solicitor General Tushar Mehta submits that suggestions from various High Courts and other stakeholders have been received and forwarded to the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Friday (October 30, 2026) asked the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) to formulate measures against the commercial exploitation of live-streamed judicial proceedings in violation of earlier court orders.

A Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant recorded Solicitor General Tushar Mehta’s submission that suggestions from various High Courts and other stakeholders had already been received and forwarded to the Ministry.
Mr. Mehta submitted that the Ministry would consider the suggestions and respond in a few days.
He sought listing of the plea for further consideration after the Deepavali vacation.
He also flagged violations of earlier orders and urged the court to consider directing the removal of material uploaded in breach of its restrictions.

The court had recently passed orders banning the unauthorised use and circulation of live-streamed judicial proceedings on social media and digital platforms, saying that anything meant for the public good cannot be exploited commercially for personal gain.
“Necessary measures for taking action against those who fail to comply with the directions will also be incorporated in the policy regime,” the court observed.

Advocate Prashant Bhushan suggested that every official clip released by the court should carry a verifiable digital signature or watermark, enabling the public and digital platforms to distinguish genuine footage from manipulated versions.
He further suggested that all court proceedings should be made available on the Supreme Court’s website in an authenticated and watermarked format.

The court is examining the issue amid concerns over the unauthorised extraction, modification, circulation, and commercial use of video clips of judicial proceedings, often accompanied by misleading captions or representations.

stories.headline: Delhi High Court Takes 'Disproportionate Burden' Off Supreme Court: CJI Surya Kant
stories.title: Delhi High Court Takes 'Disproportionate Burden' Off Supreme Court: CJI Surya Kant
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Friday said that the Delhi High Court takes a "disproportionate burden" off the Supreme Court as compared to other High Courts.

CJI said that the top court often reminds lawyers appearing before it that the Delhi High Court is "just around the corner" and that relief may be available there before their matters reach the Supreme Court.
The CJI was addressing a function organised to mark the Diamond Jubilee celebrations of the Delhi High Court, which completed 60 years.
The function was held in the Delhi High Court auditorium in S Block.

The CJI said that the High Court's location in the national capital places upon it a responsibility of extraordinary magnitude, as matters concerning governmental authority, individual liberty and public accountability regularly reach its courtrooms.
He said that the responsibilities of the Delhi High Court have multiplied with the expansion of the city, growth in commerce and increase in litigation over the years.
"What began as a court of just four judges is today an institution that resolves disputes of remarkable variety and complexity.
This High Court deserves every appreciation for rising to those demands," he said.
The CJI also highlighted the Delhi High Court's contribution to civil and commercial jurisprudence, particularly its role in developing alternative dispute resolution mechanisms.
He noted that the High Court established India's first High Court-annexed arbitration centre in 2009.

He further highlighted its original civil jurisdiction, which allows significant civil and commercial disputes to be heard directly by the High Court without litigants having to approach district courts first.
The CJI also praised the High Court's specialised Intellectual Property Division, saying that it has earned a formidable reputation in India and abroad for the quality of its jurisprudence.

stories.title: India slashed U.S. and Russian oil in September, coinciding with ‘Russia Sanctions Act’; import from UAE increases
stories.summary: Government data shows that India’s oil sourcing remains highly concentrated, with just Russia and the UAE accounting for 60% of oil imports
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: In what looks like a direct response to the ‘Russia Sanctions Act’ being signed into law that month, India in September 2026 slashed its oil imports from the U.S. to zero, and drastically cut down its imports of Russian oil, the latest official data shows.
Instead, India turned to the UAE for its oil requirement, with that country’s share rising to more than one-fourth of India’s oil imports.
As a result, India’s crude oil sourcing remains highly concentrated, with just two countries — Russia and the UAE — accounting for 60% of all oil imports.
The U.S. House of Representatives on September 16 passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which was then signed into law by President Donald Trump on September 18.
The law empowered the U.S. to levy tariffs of up to 100% on countries such as India and China that imported large quantities of Russian oil and gas.

The tariffs are currently in abeyance, with Mr. Trump on October 16 signing an executive order temporarily waiving the tariffs and submitting a certification to the U.S. Congress saying that the pause was in the U.S.’ national interest.
Indian government data on October oil imports will be released next month.
India imported 209.4 lakh tonnes of crude oil in September 2026, which was 9.5% higher than in August, and 4.1% higher than in September last year.

However, as has been the case in the last six months or so, elevated crude oil prices have meant that India’s oil import bill has swelled far faster than the growth in the actual quantity of oil being imported.

The data shows that India’s oil import bill of nearly $14.3 billion in September 2026 was 16.4% higher than the bill in August, and a much more significant 33% higher than in September 2025 when oil prices were relatively more benign.
